title: Secure logging
summary: What services must and must not write to their logs, so that incidents can be investigated without logs becoming a leak.
scope: All services and jobs that run in a company cloud project or subscription. Developer laptops are out of scope.

requirements.title: No secrets in logs
requirements.statement: Passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys and session ids are never written to logs, traces or error messages.
requirements.rationale: Logs are read by many people and copied to many systems. A secret in a log has to be treated as leaked.
guidance: Log the name of a credential, never its value.
Mask the Authorization header and cookies before logging a request.
Use the logging library's redaction list for known secret field names.

bad: fmt.Printf("request: %+v", req) // prints the Authorization header

verification.description: Secret scanner on log statements in the build pipeline, plus code review.

lookFor: A variable named like password, secret, token, apiKey or authorization passed to a log call
Whole request, header or config objects printed with %v, %+v, JSON.stringify or similar
Secrets interpolated into error messages that are later logged

requirements.title: No personal data in logs
requirements.statement: Names, email addresses, phone numbers, payment data and national ids are not logged. Use an internal id instead.
requirements.rationale: Logs are kept longer and shared wider than the systems the data came from.
guidance: Log the customer id, not the customer.
If an email is needed to investigate, log a salted hash.

bad: logger.info('order placed', { email: customer.email, card: customer.card })

lookFor: Fields named email, phone, name, address, card, iban or ssn in a log call
User or customer objects logged as a whole

requirements.title: Log security events
requirements.statement: Sign-in success and failure, permission changes and access to sensitive data are logged with who, what, when and from where.
requirements.rationale: Without these events an incident cannot be reconstructed.
guidance: Use the audit logger of the platform library; do not write your own format.
Include the acting user id, the target and the outcome.

lookFor: A new sign-in, role change or data export path with no audit log call

requirements.title: Central log shipping in production
requirements.statement: Production services send their logs to the central log platform and keep them for at least 90 days.
guidance: Use the platform's logging sidecar or agent.
Do not write logs only to local disk.

verification.description: Platform policy check on the deployment.

requirements.title: Structured logs
requirements.statement: Logs are written as structured key/value records, not free text.
requirements.rationale: Structured logs can be searched and redacted reliably.
guidance: Use the standard logger of your language: slog for Go, pino for Node.

lookFor: fmt.Println, console.log or print used for application logging
